source_ref.precedent_pattern: governance/service.py already had a `<entity>_surface_state` / `_<entity>_allowed_actions` / `<entity>_projection` seam (committee_projection, consult_memo_projection); this task adds mutation_review_projection following the same shape so it can be called from both the nested GET router and the direct POST action validators.

delivery_nature.statement: Prior to this task, main.py's POST action validators (ApproveMutation/RejectMutation/ReviewMutation/ExecuteMutation) derived allowedActions from a correct, actor/state/evidence-based `_mutation_review_projection` helper, while the GET /api/v1/operator/mutation-review/{decision_id} route (governance/router.py -> GovernanceService.mutation_review) called a second, stale nested copy that hardcoded meta.surfaces.mutation_review to the literal string 'fresh', omitted allowedActions entirely, and never failed the surface to 'unavailable' when required approval/incident/postmortem evidence was missing -- it only 404/503'd on a handful of null top-level fields. The management evolution journal (evolution/router.py bff_management_evolution_journal) was wired without any mutation_review_projection callable at all, so it fell back to its own third ad-hoc dict (fixed 'low' risk default, no allowedActions, no surface degradation). This task consolidates all three call sites onto one policy owner: GovernanceService.mutation_review_projection (governance/service.py), which owns the actor/state/evidence-derived allowedActions matrix (_MUTATION_APPROVAL_ROLES/_MUTATION_REJECTION_ROLES/_MUTATION_REVIEW_ROLES/_MUTATION_EXECUTION_ROLES, moved from main.py), the fresh/stale/unavailable surface-state derivation (read_surface_state + per-dataset dataset_source, injected the same way as the file's other *_surface_state methods), and evidence-ref redaction. The returned projection retains the full `approval_decision` object (in addition to `approval_decision_id`) exactly as the pre-existing nested copy did, so no consumer loses information as part of the consolidation. main.py's own `_mutation_review_projection(decision_id, *, identity, snapshot_at)` is now a thin wrapper that builds a GovernanceService and delegates; the four POST validators call it by decision_id instead of pre-fetching decision/approval/incident/postmortem themselves. governance/router.py's GET endpoint calls the same method and returns a JSONResponse with a sibling top-level `surfaces` key (not nested under `error.details`) when the mutation_review surface is 'unavailable', matching the required 503 envelope shape. evolution/router.py's journal composition now calls `mutation_review_projection(decision_id, identity=..., snapshot_at=...)` (single-arg canonical API) and only falls back to its own ad-hoc dict when no projection callable is injected at all (preserving the existing standalone-router unit test path in tests/test_evolution_router.py, which is untouched and out of this task's declared write-set). evolution_journal_surfaces() gained a composed `management_evolution_journal` surface entry (source: bff_composed) alongside the existing per-dataset surfaces. The camelCase `mutationReview` alias on journal mutation-review items was deleted (canonical `mutation_review` / `record` only).
